% Pattern: kind/macro-title. LyX writes the title of a theorem as a macro,
% defined with \providecommand after the declaration.
% Seen in the gold pilot (set E).
% want thm-1 statement/theorem 1 status=here
% want proof-1 proof - proves=thm-1
% want prop-1 statement/proposition 2 status=none
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsthm}
\newtheorem{thm}{\protect\theoremname}
\newtheorem{prop}[thm]{\protect\propositionname}
\providecommand{\theoremname}{Theorem}
\providecommand{\propositionname}{Proposition}
\begin{document}
\begin{thm}
A statement.
\end{thm}
\begin{proof}
A step.
\end{proof}
\begin{prop}
Another statement.
\end{prop}
\end{document}
